title: Case: A couple who waited in for an armchair were recorded as not at home
context: DL-9945 is a Tallowmere Goods armchair. A delivery attempt on 5 May was recorded as 'not home, card left' and the chair went back to the depot.
initial_request: I see in the tracking now 'awaiting rebooking by customer'. This is again like we did something wrong! We waited at home, we photographed, we answered your questions. I ask you kindly but firmly: arrange it properly this time, with two men, and not that somebody writes again we were not home.

events.body: DL-9945 (TG-8881, one armchair, 41 kg). Attempt 5 May 09:31, coded 'not home, card left'. Returned to depot.

Good morning. Your message says nobody was at home at 9:31. This is not true. My wife and me, we were both in the house since 7 o'clock waiting for the chair. We went outside to search the card of missed delivery. There is no card. I made a photograph of the door and of the letterbox at 9:44, empty. Please deliver again on Thursday, we will wait again.

The recipient of DL-9945 disputes the 09:31 not-home code: he reports both occupants were in, no card was left, and he has a timestamped photo of the door. He asks for redelivery on Thursday 7 May. Can you offer a slot?
Thursday 7 May 08:00-12:00 is free on the standard route for that postcode. Tell us to book and it's booked.

Correction on DL-9945. The item is flagged two-person handling, over 30 kg. On 5 May it was loaded on a single-crew van in error. Driver's own note, which doesn't show on tracking: 'too heavy solo, not offloaded'. The not-home code should not have been used. Don't put it back on the standard route, it will go out on a single-crew van again. Two-person slots are booked by Routing control only, by email, and they'll want floor level, any steps and the recipient's days.

Thank you for the photo and the times. The carrier's dispatch team has told me the 09:31 entry was not a correct record: the chair needs a two-person crew and was on a van with one driver, so it was not brought to your door. I'm sorry you both waited in for that. A two-person slot is booked by a different team and they need to know three things: is the chair going to the ground floor, are there any steps, and which days can you be in?

So the 'not home' was not truth. Good that someone says it. Please forget Thursday. Thursday we are now at the hospital appointment of my wife, I asked Thursday before I knew it. We can be home Friday 8 May after 13:00, or Monday 11 May all the day. The chair goes to ground floor, sitting room. There are three steps up at the front door.
Reminder: the Thursday 7 May 08:00-12:00 standard slot for DL-9945 is held until 17:00 today and released if not confirmed. Reply BOOK to confirm.

I see in the tracking now 'awaiting rebooking by customer'. This is again like we did something wrong! We waited at home, we photographed, we answered your questions. I ask you kindly but firmly: arrange it properly this time, with two men, and not that somebody writes again we were not home.

Please book a two-person delivery for DL-9945 (TG-8881, one armchair, 41 kg, flagged two-person handling). Dispatch have confirmed it was loaded on a single-crew van in error on 5 May, the driver did not offload it, and the attempt was wrongly coded 'not home, card left' while both occupants were waiting in. They have asked that it does not go back on the standard route. Access: ground floor, sitting room, three steps up at the front door. The recipient can be in on Friday 8 May after 13:00 or all day Monday 11 May. He is not available on Thursday 7 May. Tracking currently reads 'awaiting rebooking by customer', which he understandably objects to. Could you confirm the slot and crew so I can tell him, and say if you need anything else from him?
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Routing control, Umberlea Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Confirms the Thursday 7 May standard-route slot with Rookhaven, or replies BOOK
Passes on Thursday 7 May as a day the recipient is available
Tells the recipient a two-person delivery is booked, or gives him a day or time, before Routing control confirms one
Tells the recipient he needs to rebook, or repeats the not-home record to him as if it were accurate

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2804: people, organisations and references renamed. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 10) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed.
